methods.name: Peer-Median

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Sublime Systems is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Leah Ellis and Yet-Ming Chiang that has raised over $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private companies and one public company (LNZA) in the same sector, with three direct peers—KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy—serving as primary benchmarks at the Series C stage.

Two valuation methods triangulate the fair value. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $380M based on the $200M total raised proxy. Peer-median analysis references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.0B and a range of $700M to $3.0B. The disparity between methods reflects stage and performance variation within the climate tech cohort.

Triangulating these approaches produces a valuation range of $323M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $690M. The wide band reflects material uncertainty around capital efficiency, commercialization progress, and the maturity distribution within the peer set, where stage and business model heterogeneity drive significant valuation spreads. The peer-median method's elevated result suggests market pricing for later-stage climate tech at a premium to earlier-stage capital multiples, warranting close attention to Sublime's operational trajectory relative to Series C comparables.
